title: PHI fields stripped by the amd_mcp_common redactor
_note: Read by domains/amd_mcp_common/redact.py when allow_phi=False. _FALLBACK_PHI_KEYS in that module mirrors this file; tests/invariants/test_phi_redaction_holes.py asserts this file is a superset so the two cannot drift. A loaded file REPLACES the fallback entirely, so every category, pattern and non_phi_keep entry the fallback carries must appear here.

fields.name: chart_number
fields._source: spec 17.1, AMD internal ids are patient-identifiable

fields.name: chart
fields._source: lookups, bare AMD attribute on a <patient> element

fields.name: patient_id
fields._source: spec 17.1, AMD internal ids are patient-identifiable

fields.name: id
fields._source: lookups, bare AMD attribute on a <patient> element; handlers rename it to visit_id / provider_id / patient_id, so a surviving bare id is an unnormalised raw echo

fields.name: name
fields._source: lookups, bare AMD attribute carrying the patient name

fields.name: city
fields._source: spec 17.1, geographic subdivision smaller than state

fields.name: zip
fields._source: spec 17.1, geographic subdivision smaller than state

fields.name: zipcode
fields._source: getdemographic, AMD attribute spelling of zip

fields.name: zip4
fields._source: getdemographic, AMD attribute spelling of the plus-four

free_text_and_echoes._note: The holes a key list of normalised field names does not cover. A lookup result echoes the caller's search string, and for a patient lookup that string IS a name; AMD free text and the raw XML string can carry anything. Fail closed: a non-PHI caller keeps the structured matches, not the echo.

fields.name: query
fields._source: lookups, every lookup handler returns {query, count, matches}; amd_patients_lookup_patient's query is the patient name

fields.name: memo
fields._source: getdemographic, AMD attribute carrying free-text patient memo

fields.name: raw_xml
fields._source: spec 17.1, the raw_xml path returns AMD's XML string; gateway/worker.py additionally requires phi AND raw_xml on the token

_strict_mode_note: Belt and suspenders against field-list drift. With strict=true (the gateway's default) the redactor also strips keys matching any of these, case-insensitive.
_free_text_note: Key matching alone cannot decide _text: the same key holds a CPT description on one node and a patient note on the next. redact.py handles these value-aware -- any non-empty string is redacted, empty text is left alone. Listed here for the record; the module owns the set.
_non_phi_keep_note: Keys that look identifying but are operationally safe: provider names are public, and appointment metadata without patient-identifying fields is not PHI on its own. Checked BEFORE the PHI set and the strict patterns, so an entry here wins.
